introduction: A process can be alive but unable to serve useful requests. Kubernetes needs an explicit traffic contract: which port to use, which Pods match, and what makes a Pod ready. You will observe each link instead of inferring success from a green process indicator.

Stage03 has no external dependency, so /livez is also sufficient for this bounded readiness experiment. When you use the PostgreSQL adapter, readiness must use /readyz while liveness stays /livez. Do not let a transient database failure restart every application process.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 Bash in WSL2 or a disposable Linux VM; Docker is running. Use the same terminal unless a step names a second terminal.
Week25 cluster and app.yaml retained. In each new terminal set KUBECONFIG to ~/dev-opps-lab/k8s/kubeconfig; context must be kind-devopps.

concepts.title: A Service is a stable selection rule
paragraphs: A ClusterIP Service gets a stable virtual address and DNS name. Its selector finds Pod labels. EndpointSlices describe matching addresses and readiness. kube-proxy or the networking implementation routes ordinary Service connections to eligible endpoints.
kubectl port-forward service/... selects a backing Pod and creates a debugging tunnel. It does not test the normal in-cluster Service dataplane, so use a request from a second Pod as well.
concepts.example: taskboard.devopps.svc.cluster.local names a Service, not a particular Pod.
concepts.judgment: An empty EndpointSlice can mean a wrong selector or unready matching Pods. Check both before blaming DNS.

concepts.title: Three probes, three decisions
paragraphs: Startup protects initialization by postponing liveness/readiness evaluation until startup succeeds. Readiness removes a Pod from normal Service traffic without restarting it. Liveness restarts a stuck container after repeated failures.

Termination first removes serving eligibility; applications still need time to complete in-flight work. A graceful Uvicorn shutdown is useful, but an abrupt node failure cannot guarantee every in-flight request finishes.
concepts.example: A missing /readyz route produces404; a restart may leave the route equally missing.
concepts.judgment: Set thresholds from observed startup/shutdown duration and dependency behavior. Extremely aggressive liveness probes can turn overload into a restart storm.

steps.title: Declare routing and health
steps.purpose: Persist the additions rather than leaving only imperative changes.

commands.code:
export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s/kubeconfig"
kubectl config current-context
cd "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s"
kubectl -n devopps expose deployment taskboard --name=taskboard --port=80 --target-port=http --dry-run=client -o yaml > service.yaml
kubectl apply -f service.yaml
cat > probes.json <<'JSON'
{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30,"containers":[{"name":"app","startupProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/livez","port":"http"},"periodSeconds":2,"failureThreshold":30},"readinessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/livez","port":"http"},"periodSeconds":3,"failureThreshold":2},"livenessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/livez","port":"http"},"periodSeconds":10,"failureThreshold":3}}]}}}}
JSON
kubectl patch --local -f app.yaml --type=strategic --patch-file probes.json -o yaml > app-probed.yaml
kubectl apply -f app-probed.yaml
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
explain: expose generates a Service from the Deployment selector. --dry-run=client prints YAML instead of creating it; > stores that document. target-port http resolves the container's named port8000.
The JSON patch adds health timing and a30-second termination window. --local modifies the file, --type=strategic merges the container named app, and -o yaml writes a complete reproducible manifest.
Startup allows roughly60seconds for initialization. Readiness checks every3seconds and liveness every10; these are explicit lab values, not universal production defaults.
commands.expected: Service port80 maps to named app port8000; rollout reaches2/2.
commands.troubleshoot: Check the event reason and HTTP path on failing probes. A404 is different from a connection refusal.

steps.checkpoint: The original desired Deployment plus probe configuration is now app-probed.yaml.

steps.title: Follow a real Service request
steps.purpose: Observe DNS and readiness from inside the cluster.

commands.code:
kubectl -n devopps run client --image=busybox:1.37 --restart=Never --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl -n devopps wait --for=condition=Ready pod/client --timeout=120s
kubectl -n devopps exec client -- nslookup taskboard
kubectl -n devopps exec client -- wget -qO- http://taskboard/livez
kubectl -n devopps get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=taskboard -o yaml
explain: run creates one disposable client Pod; --restart=Never prevents a Deployment controller. sleep keeps the shell available. wait requires Ready.
exec runs after -- inside that Pod. nslookup asks cluster DNS. wget -qO- hides progress and writes the body to stdout. EndpointSlice selection shows addresses and conditions.ready.
commands.troubleshoot: If nslookup fails inspect kube-system DNS Pods; if DNS resolves but wget fails inspect selector and endpoint readiness before changing network policy.

steps.checkpoint: Record Service selector, matching labels, targetPort and two endpoint addresses.

steps.title: Measure a rollout
steps.purpose: Run the request loop in a second terminal; trigger the update in the first.

commands.code: kubectl -n devopps exec client -- sh -c 'i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do date -u +%FT%TZ; wget -T 2 -qO- http://taskboard/livez || echo REQUEST_FAILED; i=$((i+1)); sleep 1; done'
explain: The shell loop sends40 bounded requests with a2-second timeout. || records failures; the arithmetic increments the counter and sleep controls rate. Keep the output as evidence.
commands.expected: One timestamp/body per second; count every REQUEST_FAILED rather than hiding them.
commands.troubleshoot: Do not infer zero downtime from a final healthy state; record the whole window.

commands.code:
kubectl -n devopps rollout restart deployment/taskboard
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
explain: restart changes a Pod-template annotation to exercise replacement; it is not an image promotion. rollout status watches completion.
commands.expected: New Pods become ready before old replicas terminate under the default rolling strategy.
commands.troubleshoot: Use describe deployment and events if available replicas drop. Compare termination time with the request stream.

steps.checkpoint: Record restart behavior, then repeat the same request stream during the real digest promotion below.

steps.title: Promote a tested image by digest
steps.purpose: Use the CI artifact record from the earlier pipeline level; keep the same stage03 command so the change isolates image delivery.

commands.code:
read -r -p "New tested Taskboard IMAGE_REF from CI: " NEW_IMAGE_REF
case "$NEW_IMAGE_REF" in *@sha256:*) ;; *) printf "Use a real CI-tested digest\n"; exit 1;; esac
REGISTRY_HOST="${NEW_IMAGE_REF%%/*}"
read -r -p "Read-only GitLab deploy-token username: " REGISTRY_USER
read -r -s -p "Read-only deploy token: " REGISTRY_TOKEN; printf "\n"
kubectl -n devopps create secret docker-registry registry-read --docker-server="$REGISTRY_HOST" --docker-username="$REGISTRY_USER" --docker-password="$REGISTRY_TOKEN" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
unset REGISTRY_TOKEN
kubectl -n devopps patch deployment taskboard --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"registry-read"}]}}}}'
kubectl -n devopps set image deployment/taskboard app="$NEW_IMAGE_REF"
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
kubectl -n devopps get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}{"\n"}{end}'
explain: Read the actual new digest from a passing CI artifact. The limited registry token lets kubelet pull only the intended repository; the Secret is sent through a pipe rather than saved as a YAML file. The token is briefly a process argument during this local command: use a dedicated short-lived read-only deploy token and never publish shell traces.

The imagePullSecrets patch attaches that named credential. set image changes the desired immutable reference; rollout status and runtime image IDs verify delivery. The existing stage03 entry point stays unchanged.
commands.expected: The request stream records real behavior during an image change. Runtime IDs resolve to the promoted image or its platform-specific manifest.
commands.troubleshoot: ImagePullBackOff requires checking registry hostname, token scope and digest; do not replace the digest with latest or grant write_registry.

steps.checkpoint: Compare failure count and readiness timing with the restart experiment. Record source commit, tested digest and observed runtime image IDs.

failure.title: Distinguish a selector error from a readiness error
failure.boundary: Only this namespace; restore the first fault fully before the second.

explain: The merge patch changes the Service selector to match no application Pods.
inject.expected: Service requests fail although Pods remain Ready.

investigate.code:
kubectl -n devopps get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n devopps get service taskboard -o yaml
kubectl -n devopps get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=taskboard
explain: Compare selected labels and endpoint membership.
investigate.expected: No selected Taskboard endpoint despite healthy Pods.
investigate.troubleshoot: A cached connection can outlive a change; open a fresh wget request.

hints: Readiness controls matching Pods; it cannot fix an incorrect selector.

explanation: The Service selected the wrong population. After recovering it, change the readiness path to /missing with set probe through a copied app-probed.yaml and observe matched-but-unready endpoints. Restore app-probed.yaml afterward.

recover.troubleshoot: Inspect EndpointSlice readiness before retrying the user request.

verification.code: kubectl -n devopps exec client -- wget -qO- http://taskboard/livez
explain: A new request tests the normal Service route.
verification.troubleshoot: If no endpoint returns inspect rollout readiness.

questions.prompt: Why not probe the database from liveness?
questions.answer: A database outage affects every replica; restarting all of them adds connection churn and destroys warm capacity. Readiness and user-facing errors describe dependency availability.

questions.prompt: Does successful port-forward prove Service routing?
questions.hint: Which endpoint does the tunnel choose?
questions.answer: No. It selects a Pod for debugging; cluster DNS, selectors, virtual-IP routing and policy still require an in-cluster test.

questions.prompt: Why is a startup probe useful?
questions.answer: It gives a bounded initialization window while retaining strict liveness timing after startup; simply making all liveness checks slow also delays real failure detection.

exercise.brief: Diagnose a bad readiness path independently.
constraints: Use a copied manifest and /missing; keep liveness /livez.
Restore the known good file before leaving.
acceptance: Failure is identified as readiness, not image or scheduling
Recovery produces a fresh successful Service request
hints: kubectl describe pod shows probe HTTP status.
solution: Copy app-probed.yaml to app-not-ready.yaml, change only readinessProbe.httpGet.path to /missing, apply, inspect events/endpoints, then reapply app-probed.yaml.

explain: Delete the temporary request client. Retain Service and Deployment manifests for the next lesson.
cleanup.troubleshoot: If already absent, get pod client confirms no leftover workload.

cleanup.code:
kubectl apply -f "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s/app-probed.yaml"
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
explain: Restore the recorded local image baseline for week 27 after keeping the promotion evidence. The read-only pull Secret is deliberately retained for later registry work.
cleanup.expected: The original local baseline is healthy.
cleanup.troubleshoot: If your CI image changes the API contract, do not assume an image rollback also restores database compatibility; this stage03 exercise has no database.

repoConnections.principle: A known health interface exposes platform behavior.
repoConnections.application: Compare this probe contract to podinfo health/ready routes; transfer the mechanism to Taskboard while keeping dependency and business tests separate.

notes: Documentation-checked; Kubernetes execution remains for the learner environment.
title: Traffic, probes and safe rollout
outcome: Route requests to ready application instances and handle startup and shutdown correctly.
